description: Reviewed manifest for the Exercise II regression modelling table: the ABIDE-II FreeSurfer brain-feature table (Yarkoni NeuroHackademy tutorial) merged with the ABIDE-II phenotypic CSV. Single source of truth for scripts/abide_modeling_data.py, scripts/export_regression_catalog.py, the Exercise II notebook, and their tests. Change here, regenerate, re-test.

source.license: CC-BY-4.0 (repository LICENSE.md; the tu-machine-learning-yarkoni folder adds no separate licence)

brain_table.name: abide2.tsv
brain_table.note: 1004 participants, 1004 unique `subject` ids, no duplicates. Trailing empty header field is ignored. 6 non-brain columns + 1440 brain features. Zero missingness in the brain features.

phenotype_table.name: abide2_phenotypic.csv
phenotype_table.note: The same ABIDE-II phenotypic file Exercise I uses. Provides the cognitive / behavioural target columns that abide2.tsv lacks.

merge.note: Every one of the 1004 brain-table participants is present in the phenotypic file (0 unmatched). The merged modelling table is 1004 rows.

atlas.name: HCP-MMP1.0 (Glasser et al. 2016)
atlas.reference: Glasser MF, Coalson TS, Robinson EC, et al. A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature. 2016;536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933
atlas.hemisphere_encoding: single letter L or R immediately after the measurement prefix
atlas.preprocessing_note: FreeSurfer-derived surface metrics summarised per HCP-MMP1 parcel. No further normalisation is applied in abide2.tsv; the notebook standardises features inside the training fold only.

age.label: Age at scan
age.meaning: Age at scan in years; a native column of abide2.tsv itself (no phenotypic-file join needed) and the Yarkoni tutorial's own target.
age.structural_note: Present for every one of the 1004 participants with usable brain data; 0 missing. Spans childhood through late adulthood (5.1-64.0 yr) across all 17 sites.
age.rationale: WP12 audit (scripts/regression_model_audit.py --run; book/config/regression_model_audit_result.json): age has reliably positive out-of-sample R2 with ordinary linear regression, unlike every FIQ configuration tested (all negative). WP12 5.4 policy: a target with reliably positive out-of-sample R2 becomes the main ordinary-linear-regression example. It also needs no join (available for all 1004 brain-table rows, not 908) and lets the leakage/scoring and sample-size sections use a signal that is actually there to lose to overfitting, rather than one that is not.

FIQ.label: Full-scale IQ (FIQ)
FIQ.meaning: Full-scale IQ (composite standard score; the exact test instrument varies by site and is not recorded per row in the merged 1004 - FIQ_TEST_TYPE is entirely empty here).
FIQ.structural_note: Present at 16 of 17 sites; missing entirely only at ABIDEII-EMC_1 (n=53). Balanced across diagnosis (autism 423, control 485).
FIQ.rationale: WP11 established FIQ is barely predictable from cortical morphometry in this sample (every tested feature set gives negative held-out/cross-validated R2 under ordinary least squares). WP12 keeps FIQ as a compact secondary example specifically to show, honestly, whether ridge or lasso regularisation can turn a broad brain-wide feature space from underdetermined-and-useless into something at or above zero -- see protocol.regularisation_preview. It is deliberately not the main worked example: WP12 5.4 says a target whose regularised score remains at or below zero must be reported as such, not promoted.

rejected_targets.VIQ: IQ subscale; FIQ is a composite of VIQ and PIQ, so pairing VIQ against FIQ is leakage-adjacent and pedagogically confusing.
rejected_targets.PIQ: IQ subscale; same reason as VIQ.
rejected_targets.ADOS_G_TOTAL: n=306 but ~87% autism group and near-absent at several sites (SDSU_1 0, OHSU_1 3, UCD_1 1, NYU_2 1); essentially confined to one diagnostic group and a handful of sites.
rejected_targets.ADI_R_SOCIAL_TOTAL_A: n=285, 0 controls; structurally an autism-only instrument, so a performance difference would be uninterpretable.
rejected_targets.SRS_TOTAL_RAW: WP11's lower-availability secondary target (n=764, both diagnostic groups, 13/17 sites) for a FIQ-vs-SRS availability contrast. That contrast no longer has a role once age (n=1004, 0 missing) is the main target and FIQ is the regularisation-preview secondary target (WP12 5.4/6.4); the WP12 audit did not re-test SRS_TOTAL_RAW as a candidate main target because it is a phenotype column requiring the same join as FIQ, with materially lower availability, and no literature framing distinct from FIQ. Still fetched by the merge (source.merge.phenotype_columns_kept) and available for a future exercise.

leakage_guard.principle: Every column of the model input matrix X must match atlas.column_pattern and name an ROI in roi_label_inventory. Nothing else may enter X.

protocol.preprocessing: sklearn Pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression()); the scaler is fitted on training rows / training folds only. No imputation is needed - the brain features have no missing values and rows missing the target are dropped before splitting.
protocol.generalisation_target: Held-out participants drawn from the same 17 ABIDE-II sites. A random participant split does NOT estimate generalisation to unseen scanners or sites.

canonical_recipe.note: Bilateral cortical thickness across every eligible cortical region (p=358). Age-related cortical thinning is a whole-cortex phenomenon (Bethlehem et al. 2022; Storsve et al. 2014), not one a small literature-specified regional bundle would represent fairly, so the canonical recipe uses the full eligible ROI set for one measure rather than a hand-picked subset. p=358 stays well under n_train (~803 at the full holdout split, ~726 at 5-fold), so ordinary least squares is well posed.

regularisation_preview.purpose: WP12 6.1: a short, honest demonstration of what happens when p is comparable to or exceeds n_train, and whether ridge / lasso stabilise it, for BOTH targets.
regularisation_preview.note: p=1432 exceeds n_train at every split used in this manifest (holdout ~753-681, 5-fold ~803-726), so ordinary least squares is underdetermined for both age and FIQ here (diagnostic only, never the recommended model). Ridge and lasso are fitted with StandardScaler inside the pipeline and their alpha is chosen by an inner cross-validation on the training partition only - never by consulting held-out or outer-CV score.

catalog.identifiability_rule: An entry is offered only if its feature count p is below 0.7 * (fold training n). all-eligible x [CT,Area] (p=716) and any entry with p >= that bound is disabled with a visible reason rather than fitted with a pseudo-inverse.
catalog.note: The interactive feature-set comparison activity offers ordinary least squares only, never regularised models; that restriction is about this activity being unregularised OLS, not about p vs n in general (WP12 6.3) - the separate regularisation-preview computation (protocol.regularisation_preview) is where ridge / lasso are used, on the full p=1432 space, computed directly in the notebook rather than exposed as extra activity controls. Trying many entries here is still exploratory model comparison; the cross-validation score of the best-looking entry is not an unbiased estimate of its performance.

canonical_recipe.note: Identical to protocol.canonical_recipe (p=358), reused so Exercise 3's KNN result is directly comparable to Exercise 2's OLS result: same participants, split, target, and feature set.

cv_for_k_selection.note: Selects k on the outer-TRAINING partition only (753 rows); Exercise 2's own documented cross-validation protocol, reused verbatim.

dev_split.note: Further splits the outer-TRAINING partition (753 rows) into a fitting subset (n_fit=564) and a validation subset (n_val=189) for the empirical all-k curve (Exercise 3 section 4.5) and the interactive activity (section 4.6). Independent of, and never touching, the outer test set (251 rows) locked by protocol.holdout_split.

knn.selected_k_rationale: WP13 audit (scripts/knn_model_audit.py --run): 5-fold CV on the outer-training partition only, canonical all-eligible x CT recipe (p=358); k=15 maximises mean CV R2 (+0.598) over a log-spaced grid spanning 1..602 (the largest k valid inside that CV). Locked held-out test R2=+0.647 (MSE 32.99), evaluated exactly once after k was already fixed -- higher than the two smaller predeclared bundles tested (frontoparietal p=78: k*=82, test R2=+0.477; occipital p=46: k*=20, test R2=+0.425) and higher than Exercise 2's OLS result (R2=+0.475) on the identical participants/split/target/features. No curse-of-dimensionality problem was observed for standardized KNN on this canonical recipe, so the canonical feature set is retained (not a smaller bundle) both for the cleanest result and so the Exercise 2 comparison is apples-to-apples.

frontoparietal.label: Frontoparietal (P-FIT)
frontoparietal.literature: Jung & Haier (2007) Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (BA 9/45/46/47), inferior/superior parietal lobule and intraparietal sulcus (BA 7/39/40), and dorsal anterior cingulate (BA 32).

frontal.label: Prefrontal only
frontal.literature: The prefrontal component of P-FIT and of Narr et al. (2007): dorsolateral / inferior frontal cortex plus dorsal anterior cingulate, with no parietal ROIs.

parietal.label: Parietal only
parietal.literature: The parietal component of P-FIT: inferior parietal lobule (PG*, PF*), intraparietal sulcus (IP*, IPS1, LIP*, MIP, VIP, AIP) and superior parietal lobule (area 7 subdivisions).

temporal.label: Lateral temporal (comparison)
temporal.literature: Lateral / superior temporal cortex. Narr et al. (2007) reported some temporal thickness-IQ associations, so this is a scoped anatomical comparison, not a null region.

occipital.label: Occipital / early visual (comparison)
occipital.literature: Primary and extrastriate visual cortex. Not part of P-FIT's core; included as a similarly sized anatomical comparison bundle.

sensorimotor.label: Sensorimotor (comparison)
sensorimotor.literature: Primary and premotor / somatosensory cortex. A similarly sized non-association-cortex comparison bundle.

pfit.citation: Jung RE, Haier RJ. The Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory (P-FIT) of intelligence: converging neuroimaging evidence. Behav Brain Sci. 2007;30(2):135-154.

narr.citation: Narr KL, Woods RP, Thompson PM, et al. Relationships between IQ and regional cortical gray matter thickness in healthy adults. Cereb Cortex. 2007;17(9):2163-2171.
